intro: Roaming lets a driver charge with one card on the chargers of many companies, as a phone works on other networks abroad. OCPI connects the charge point operator (CPO), who runs the chargers, with the e-mobility service provider (eMSP), who gives drivers their cards and apps. Each side offers a REST API: a set of web addresses that the other side calls to read or send data. Through them they share charger locations, cards, charging sessions, and the bill for each charge.
plain: With one card or app, you can charge your electric car on chargers run by many different companies, much like your phone works on other networks when you travel abroad. For that, the company that runs the charger and the company that gave you your card must work together. This is the language their computer systems use to share where the chargers are, check that your card is valid, and send each other the bill.

discover.title: First contact
discover.text: Two companies connect once, before any driver roams. The eMSP reads which OCPI versions the CPO offers, and the web address of each part (module) of its API.

register.title: Swap access tokens
register.text: A token is a secret string, like a password, sent with every request. The eMSP registers with a temporary token, A. Then each side has its own token for calling the other: the eMSP calls the CPO with token C, and the CPO calls the eMSP with token B.

location.title: Publish a charger
location.text: The CPO sends a location (a charging site) with one EVSE: one charging point. Now the eMSP's app can show it to drivers.

authorize.title: Check a card
authorize.text: A driver with a card from the eMSP taps it on the charger. The CPO does not know this card, so it asks the eMSP whether it may charge.

session.title: Charging session
session.text: Charging starts. The CPO reports the session (this one charge), then sends updates while the car charges.

cdr.title: Send the bill
cdr.text: After the charge, the CPO sends the CDR (charge detail record): the final record of what the eMSP owes for this charge.

frames.versions: Which OCPI versions do you speak, and where?
frames.post-credentials: Here is token B for calling me, and my address
frames.check: Which versions do you speak? (with token B)
frames.credentials: Registered. Call me with token C from now on
frames.authorize: Card 04A2B3C4D5E6F7 at LOC-0042: may it charge?

notes.versions: The eMSP got two things from the CPO by e-mail or a portal: the URL of its versions list and token A. It reads the list with GET. The header Authorization: Token, followed by token A in Base64, proves who is asking. Then it sends GET to the URL of version 2.2.1.
notes.endpoints: Every OCPI answer has the same envelope (the same outer fields): data, status_code, status_message and timestamp. Here data first lists the versions, then the endpoints of 2.2.1: one URL per module, each marked SENDER (owns the data) or RECEIVER. The CPO is the sender of locations, sessions and CDRs, and the receiver of tokens.
notes.post-credentials: Still with token A, the eMSP posts its own credentials: a new token B for the CPO to use, the URL of its own versions list, and its role: EMSP, country_code DE, party_id XYZ (its company code).
notes.check: Before it answers, the CPO checks the eMSP the same way: GET its versions, then its 2.2.1 endpoints, with token B.
notes.credentials: The CPO answers with its credentials: token C, its versions URL, and its role: CPO, country_code NL, party_id ABC. Token A stops working. From now on the eMSP calls with token C and the CPO with token B.
notes.put-location: The CPO stores the location in the eMSP's locations endpoint with PUT (create or replace). The URL names the owner and the location's id. The anatomy takes it apart, and the playground shows the body.
notes.location-ok: status_code 1000 is success. Read it, not only the HTTP status: 2xxx is a client error (the request was wrong), 3xxx a server error.
notes.authorize: Real-time authorization: the CPO asks while the driver waits. The card belongs to the eMSP, so the CPO posts to the eMSP's tokens endpoint: the card's uid in the URL, ?type=RFID, and the location and EVSE in the body.
notes.allowed: data.allowed is ALLOWED, with the card's full token object. Other answers are BLOCKED, EXPIRED, NO_CREDIT and NOT_ALLOWED. The CPO tells its charger, over OCPP, to start.
notes.put-session: The CPO creates the session on the eMSP's side: start_date_time, kwh 0, the card as cdr_token, auth_method AUTH_REQUEST, the location, EVSE and connector, currency EUR, status ACTIVE.
notes.patch-session: With PATCH, only what changed travels: kwh 6.25 and last_updated. The eMSP's app can now show the driver the energy so far.
notes.post-cdr: The CDR is the bill between the two companies: when, where, which card, how much energy and time, and the price. The playground shows it.
notes.cdr-ok: The eMSP stores the CDR and returns its own URL for it in the Location header. Now it can bill the driver.

a-country.name: Country
a-country.note: NL: the two-letter ISO 3166 code of the operator's country.

a-operator.name: Operator
a-operator.note: ABC: the operator's ID, unique in its country. In OCPI it is the CPO's party_id.

a-type.name: Type
a-type.note: E: this ID names an EVSE, a charging point.

a-evse.name: EVSE
a-evse.note: 12345*1: the operator's own number for this charging point.

u-endpoint.name: Endpoint
u-endpoint.note: The eMSP's web address for locations, taken from its list of endpoints. The CPO never builds it itself.

u-country.name: country_code
u-country.note: The country of the party that owns the object: the CPO.

u-party.name: party_id
u-party.note: The CPO's party ID. With country_code, it names a company in every OCPI object.

u-location.name: location_id
u-location.note: The CPO's id for this location. Adding /1 would address the EVSE with uid 1 inside it.

facts.between: CPO (runs chargers) ↔ eMSP (gives drivers cards and apps), directly or through a roaming hub
facts.security: TLS. Every request carries Authorization: Token, followed by the token in Base64.
facts.frames: Modules: credentials, locations, tokens, sessions, cdrs, tariffs, commands

tips: Use the URLs the other side lists in its endpoints. Never build them from a pattern: every platform has its own.
Token A works only to register. A common cause of 401 errors (access refused) after registration is mixing up tokens B and C.
HTTP 200 is not enough: read status_code in the body. 1000 is success, 2xxx a client error, 3xxx a server error.
A CDR is final. A wrong one is not changed: the CPO sends a credit CDR that cancels it, then a new one.

points.to-cpo: Token for calls to the CPO
points.to-emsp: Token for calls to the eMSP

anatomy.evse-id: An EVSE ID, as drivers see it on the charger
anatomy.url: The address of one location on the eMSP's side

playground.file: An object the CPO sends in this lesson, as JSON. Pick an underlined line.
playground.owner: The CPO that owns this location: country NL, party ABC. They are in every object, and in its URL.
playground.location-id: The CPO's own id for the location. With country_code and party_id, it is unique.
playground.publish: true: the eMSP may show it to drivers. false keeps a private charger off public maps.
playground.country: Three letters here (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3), unlike the two of country_code.
playground.coordinates: Latitude and longitude are strings, not numbers, with 5 to 7 decimals.
playground.evse-uid: uid: the CPO's internal id of the EVSE, used in URLs and in sessions.
playground.evse-id: evse_id: the ID printed on the charger, for drivers. The anatomy takes it apart.
playground.status: AVAILABLE: free to use. When it changes, the CPO sends a PATCH with the new status.
playground.standard: IEC_62196_T2: a Type 2 socket. format SOCKET means the driver brings the cable.
playground.max-voltage: 230 V: for 3-phase AC, the voltage between one phase and neutral.
playground.tariff: The tariff (price plan) that applies here. The CPO publishes it in the tariffs module.
playground.time-zone: The local time zone. Times in OCPI are UTC; this tells the app what the local clock says.
playground.last-updated: When this object last changed. A party that missed updates asks for everything changed since it last caught up.
playground.cdr-id: The CPO's id for this CDR.
playground.session-id: The session this CDR closes: the one the eMSP saw grow.
playground.cdr-token: The card that charged. It belongs to the eMSP XYZ from Germany (DE).
playground.contract: contract_id: the driver's contract with the eMSP. The eMSP bills this contract.
playground.auth-method: AUTH_REQUEST: the CPO asked the eMSP in real time. WHITELIST would mean a list of cards sent earlier.
playground.cdr-location: A copy of where it happened, so that the CDR still reads right after the location changes.
playground.currency: Every amount in this CDR is in EUR.
playground.periods: The charge, cut into periods with one tariff each. This one has a single period.
playground.dimensions: 12.5 kWh in this period. The next line: 1.25 h of time.
